effect: Four sound effects the game never plays
note: Sounds go through $34B6 (197 callers) to $B84E (EU $B848), which queues them for the Z80 at $A01C30. Neither the numbers written into those calls nor the tables at $4B58, $69B2, $9C74 and $C868 give 2E, 43, 55 or 63. 2E is a three-second effect in several parts, 43 a short sound whose data runs into 42's, 55 a short high blip and 63 a short low one. Recorded in BizHawk.

effect: An unused version of the continue screen's sprites, with big countdown digits 0-9
note: Graphics load through the list reader $94D8 (directories at $9554). Its 63 calls use fixed lists, menu and tileset tables, and lists built in RAM; none names entry 2:$14 (= 1:$34, $A059E). It is the continue screen's sheet (2:$15) with its colours renumbered, except that the small countdown digits are big outlined ones. The continue screen's frame table ($DA7CC) builds them as frames $74-$7D. Its palette, 2:$1F, is never loaded either; with the same renumbering its first line is the continue screen's palette. The image shows the digits as the frames ask, on 2:$1F's third line, a colour ramp.

effect: Bomberman '94's title screen, the planets with its logo beside them, whose logo tiles this game doesn't have
note: No load list names maps 2:$05/$06 (or 2:$03, the starfield with 23 stars moved). They are Bomberman '94's title screen, converted cell for cell: in '94, once the logo has flown in as sprites, $9C02 copies its left part into the background and these maps draw it beside the planets. Mega Bomberman has its own title and neither the logo set nor the copy routine, so its tiles $600-$6F3 are never loaded. Drawn with '94's tiles, the shape is the start of the '94 logo ("BO" on a cloud). The colours of the logo are a guess.

effect: A round blue one-eyed creature in two frames, loaded for the area 3 boss but never drawn
note: 1:$1D is loaded only by list $198D0, for the area 3 boss fight (the crab). None of the frame tables active there ($DC3D8, $D9386, $DA5EA, the players') names tiles $5F8-$5FF, and no map uses them; every other piece of the set is named. The palette line is a guess, taken from the bubbles next to it.

effect: Battle Game takes four pads through EA's 4-Way Play adapter, one player each, though the game never mentions it
note: At power-on only, $7C34 runs EA's handshake ($90F2: $43 to $A1000B, $7C to $A10005, $7F, $7C again) and, if $A10003 & 3 = 0, sets $80C2 = $FF. Every frame $7E1E then calls $912A, which selects each pad ($0C/$1C/$2C/$3C to $A10005) and reads it into the four player records ($800A/$8014/$801E/$8028). An adapter plugged in later is never seen. BizHawk (GPGX, 4-Way Play): B pressed on pads 1-4 in turn lands in battle slots 1-4 ($AD0A + 8n), one each. Also: with plain pads, players 3 and 4 copy pad 1 (all four slots start on pad 1, $103D4), so with two pads and four combatants pad 1 drives three Bombermen.

effect: If the cartridge's data doesn't match its checksum, the game shows a red screen forever
note: $7BC6-$7C04 (Europe $7BEC) sums the words from $200 to the end address in the header ($1A4) and compares the total with $18E; on a mismatch it sets colour 0 to red ($00E) and stops. The 8-player demo has no such check. BizHawk, US ROM with its last byte changed: red after 300 frames. So an IPS patch must also fix the checksum word at $18E; Game Genie codes are not affected.
